events.what: Preprint proving K1,2,2,2 has no n-fold planar cover for n<14 (later published in Graphs and Combinatorics, Nov 2025)
Three Theorems on Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture: no planar cover of K1,2,2,2 of ply below 14, and any minimal planar cover must be 4-connected
On high genus extensions of Negami's conjecture: generalisation to other compact surfaces
New combinatorial proof of the known result that rotation-compatible planar covers embed in the projective plane

judgement.doubts: The ply bound itself (n<14) first appeared in the Nov 2023 preprint, before the snapshot; the genuinely new post-snapshot content of 2412.19560 is the 4-connectivity constraint (and whatever else the third theorem is). Both are restrictions on where a hypothetical cover of K1,2,2,2 could live, not settlement of any case of the bullet, so progress either way.

corrections.why: F3: the record itself describes the Dec 2024 results as 'restrictions on the space where a hypothetical cover could live, narrowing but not closing the case'. A lower bound on the ply of a possible cover and a connectivity constraint on a minimal one settle no restriction of the bullet's question (the single remaining graph K1,2,2,2 is still undecided); they are bounds, so the tier is progress.
F14: a progress row carries no direction; nothing was settled.
